svg.title: How Cairn's AI agents went from an API map to a root shell on MONAI Label
svg.text: From API map to root shell
What Cairn's agents did to a MONAI Label server, September 2026. Red marks the zero-day. Source: Amazon Threat Intelligence.

g.text: Fingerprint the app and map its API
Agents identify MONAI Label and list its endpoints. No login needed: authentication is off by default.
Spot an upload endpoint that takes a filename, test path traversal
PUT /datastore/image and /datastore/label never check the path stays inside the datastore.
Arbitrary file write anywhere the server can write
About 11 minutes after step 1. Unknown bug at the time, now CVE-2026-133968 (CVSS 9.8).
Later session: write a reverse shell into sitecustomize.py
Python imports this file automatically every time an interpreter starts.
Call the training API, which starts a new Python process
The process loads the payload and connects back to the attacker as root.

svg.text: the operator gave the agents a proxy into a second university network, via a server running the same software.
